transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, thanks. I guess… the main thing is that I’ve been having trouble staying with things, even when I really intend to. Like, I’ll sit down with a stack of essays to mark, or a curriculum document I need to get through, and I’m ready to work, but then ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page.

It’s not that I don’t care about it—I do. I just notice my mind has gone off in three different directions, and I’ve barely taken in what’s in front of me. It’s a bit embarrassing to say, but that’s probably what pushed me to come in.
Would you say you've had this kind of trouble concentrating since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently, like in the past few months?

I think it’s been around for a long time, yeah. Not just the last few months.

I mean, I did well enough in school, so I don’t want to overstate it, but even in primary school my report cards had comments like “bright but careless” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me. And my parents used to find worksheets all crumpled up in my backpack that I’d apparently forgotten to hand in. So… yeah, I suppose it was there pretty early on.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or noticing a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I have off days like anyone, and I can get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.

I’m still enjoying things when I actually make time for them. So… no, I don’t think that’s the main issue, if that makes sense.

Would you say these attention difficulties have caused real problems for you—like at work, in relationships, or managing daily responsibilities—not just being annoying, but actually causing issues in more than one area of your life?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wish I could say it was just annoying, but it has caused actual problems.

At work, the follow-through stuff has gotten serious enough that my department chair put me on a support plan. That was… hard to admit, because I do care about doing a good job. And at home, my wife has started taking over things like bills and reminders, because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep track of them consistently.

So yes, I guess it’s more than one area. I’m not proud of that, but that’s probably the honest answer.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find it hard to sit still, or notice yourself interrupting others or acting impulsively?

Um… I wouldn’t say that’s a big thing for me, no. I mean, I might shift around in my chair or tap a pen sometimes, but I don’t think people would describe me as especially restless or unable to sit still.

And interrupting… I hope not. I probably do it occasionally like anyone, but it’s not something I’ve really noticed as a pattern. The impulsive side doesn’t feel like the main issue, if that answers it properly.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong pattern (since primary school) of inattentiveness—difficulty sustaining focus, distractibility, forgetfulness, and incomplete tasks—corroborated by childhood report card comments and behaviors. Symptoms are chronic rather than episodic, not attributable to mood disturbance (explicitly denies depressive symptoms/anhedonia), and cause significant impairment in multiple domains (occupational performance leading to a formal support plan, and marital/home functioning with spouse assuming responsibility for tasks). Hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, interrupting, impulsivity) are minimal and not a significant clinical feature, supporting a predominantly inattentive presentation consistent with ADHD (F90.0). Anxiety and depressive disorders were considered but do not fit given the chronicity, developmental onset, and absence of mood/anxiety symptom clusters.
